calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, and the Senators are one of the league’s best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Red Wings’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.5 expected goals per 60 against the Senators.
calls.nums: Detroit 4th for the power play (8.5 expected goals per 60) · Ottawa 2nd for the penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On the power play, Detroit had 12.0 per 60. The league average is 7.5 per 60, and they came in at 8.5 per 60.

calls.head: The Senators should get some good looks
calls.body: The Senators make their shots count, and the Red Wings are near the bottom of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Senators to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Senators’ average shot has at least their usual 6.8% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Ottawa 3rd for shot quality (a 6.8% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Detroit 25th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Ottawa’s average shot had a 5.3% chance of going in, against their usual 6.8%.

DET.head: We had this close to even (46% for Detroit), and Detroit came through.

OTT.head: We had this close to even (54% for Ottawa), and it went Detroit’s way.

surprises.head: Detroit brought the hits
surprises.body: Detroit’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 178, against their usual 97 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Detroit tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Copp, K. Kolesar, M. Rasmussen played 10:09 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Detroit’s usual lines.

story.head: The Red Wings beat the Senators
paras: Tim Stützle opened the scoring early in the first. Alex DeBrincat added two goals. Four different Red Wings scored. Justin Faulk scored the winner early in the second.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Red Wings tried a line they hadn’t used before: Andrew Copp, Keegan Kolesar and Michael Rasmussen.

items.text: Whether the Red Wings keep that line together at home against Seattle on Friday.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
